title: RTK Query Production Architecture and Testing Checkpoint

questions.prompt: Two feature files need coordinated Author invalidation. What is the usual starting point?

options.label: Inject endpoints into a shared base API and register its middleware once.
Create unrelated API slices with equal tag names and assume cross-slice invalidation.
Register the same API middleware once per screen.

questions.explanation: Endpoint injection preserves the shared cache/tag namespace. Equal tag names across separate APIs do not coordinate them, and duplicate middleware registration is not required.

questions.prompt: selectFromResult returns a newly filtered array each time. Why can rerenders persist?

options.label: The outer result object is forbidden from being newly allocated.
selectFromResult guarantees no component ever rerenders.
The selected array reference changes; memoize derived collections or select stable values.

questions.explanation: The returned fields are compared shallowly. A fresh nested array changes a field reference; a new outer object with stable fields is expected, and real selected changes must still rerender.

questions.prompt: Which lifecycle is suitable for a stream tied to cached data?

options.label: Keep the HTTP queryFn unresolved forever to represent socket lifetime.
onCacheEntryAdded with validated events and cleanup after cacheEntryRemoved.
Open a new socket in every render and never close it.

questions.explanation: Cache-entry lifecycle work can own a stream and clean it up. Render-driven sockets leak/duplicate work; a permanently pending HTTP query confuses query completion and can delay invalidation.

questions.prompt: What avoids sharing one visitor’s Redux state with another in Next.js?

options.label: Request-safe store/provider boundaries and client-owned RTK Query usage.
A server-global mutable Redux store reused for all requests.
Move access tokens into serializable query keys to authorize server rendering.

questions.explanation: A server-global store can leak request state. Follow request-safe boundaries and server/client ownership; cache keys are not authorization and must not contain tokens.

questions.prompt: Why might refetchOnFocus work on web but not on React Native?

options.label: RTK Query supports only desktop web.
Increasing keepUnusedDataFor emits native focus events.
Native lifecycle/connectivity signals need appropriate custom listener integration.

questions.explanation: Browser listener defaults do not supply native AppState/connectivity integration. RTK can run in native apps, and cache retention settings do not create lifecycle events.

questions.prompt: Which setup can prove tag invalidation actually refetches?

options.label: Assert the component imported a hook with the right name.
A real configured store with controlled transport and assertions on requests and final data.
Mock every query hook to return the expected post-mutation response.

questions.explanation: A real store exercises endpoint arguments, middleware, subscriptions, and tags. Mocked hook data or import assertions bypass the mechanism and cannot prove refetch behavior.
